question: State Huygens principle. Explain why every point on a wavefront can be treated as a source of secondary wavelets.

options.A: Huygens principle states that only the original source emits secondary wavelets; a wavefront cannot transfer disturbance to nearby points.
options.B: Huygens principle states that every point of a wavefront emits rays only in the forward direction, and the centres of these rays form the next wavefront.
options.C: Huygens principle states that every point on a given wavefront acts as a source of secondary wavelets spreading in all directions with the speed of light in the medium. Their forward envelope at a later instant gives the new wavefront. Since points on a wavefront are in the same phase, each can transfer the disturbance to neighbouring points and act as a secondary source.
options.D: Huygens principle states that wavefronts travel only as rigid planes, so no point on a wavefront acts as a source.
